mythsVsFacts.myth: Repeats are automatic forever.
mythsVsFacts.fact: GP authorisation expires and must be renewed periodically.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Pharmacy can authorise new repeats.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Only the GP can authorise repeat prescriptions.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Reorder on the day you run out.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Reorder 7–10 days early to avoid gaps.

mythsVsFacts.myth: EPS works without nomination.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Nomination must be set with your GP surgery.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Repeats skip clinical checks.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Every supply includes clinical screening.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Hospital medicines are always on repeat.
mythsVsFacts.fact: GP may need to add hospital-started medicines to repeats.

mythsVsFacts.myth: You can collect unlimited early supply.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Supply timing follows prescription dates and CD rules.

mythsVsFacts.myth: All items on slip are always ready together.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Partial supply occurs when items need ordering.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Changing pharmacy breaks repeats permanently.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Update EPS nomination when switching pharmacy.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Repeat means no GP review needed.
mythsVsFacts.fact: GP reviews remain essential for ongoing conditions.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Repeat Prescriptions replaces all GP care.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Repeat Prescriptions complements GP services — chronic and complex conditions remain with your GP.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Every patient automatically qualifies for Repeat Prescriptions.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Individual clinical assessment confirms suitability for repeat prescriptions.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Repeat Prescriptions is always free.
mythsVsFacts.fact: NHS eligibility and commissioning determine cost — private repeat prescriptions may incur disclosed fees.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Walk-in guarantees immediate Repeat Prescriptions.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Booking may be required; clinical assessment always precedes supply.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Online research removes the need for Repeat Prescriptions.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Personalised assessment and supply decisions require a pharmacist consultation.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Repeat Prescriptions treats emergencies.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Emergencies need 999 or A&E — repeat prescriptions is not an emergency service.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Side effects from Repeat Prescriptions should be ignored.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Report side effects promptly to the pharmacy or GP.

mythsVsFacts.myth: All pharmacies offer identical Repeat Prescriptions.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Commissioning, training and private service menus vary locally.

mythsVsFacts.myth: No follow-up is needed after Repeat Prescriptions.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Safety-netting and review are essential parts of safe care.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Repeat Prescriptions always includes medicine supply.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Advice-only outcomes are valid when supply is not clinically appropriate.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Pharmacists are not qualified for Repeat Prescriptions.
mythsVsFacts.fact: GPhC-registered pharmacists deliver repeat prescriptions under clinical governance.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Repeat Prescriptions is the same as a GP appointment.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Repeat Prescriptions operates within defined pharmacy scope with referral when needed.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Sharing Repeat Prescriptions medicines is acceptable.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Prescription medicines are individualised — never share.

mythsVsFacts.myth: Repeat Prescriptions needs no preparation.
mythsVsFacts.fact: Some appointments require specific preparation — confirm at booking.

mythsVsFacts.myth: NHS and private Repeat Prescriptions are identical.
mythsVsFacts.fact: NHS pathways have eligibility criteria; private scope may differ.

faqLibrary.question: When should I reorder repeat prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Reorder 7–10 days before medicines run out, or earlier for items needing ordering. The pharmacy team provides evidence-based guidance tailored to your situation, with clear safety-netting before you leave.

faqLibrary.question: How do I set up EPS nomination?
faqLibrary.answer: Nominate your pharmacy with your GP surgery — prescriptions then flow electronically. The pharmacy team provides evidence-based guidance tailored to your situation, with clear safety-netting before you leave.

faqLibrary.question: What if my repeat is not authorised?
faqLibrary.answer: The pharmacy liaises with your surgery — allow extra time for GP authorisation. The pharmacy team provides evidence-based guidance tailored to your situation, with clear safety-netting before you leave.

faqLibrary.question: Can I get extra supply for holiday?
faqLibrary.answer: GP authorisation may be needed — request holiday supply early. The pharmacy team provides evidence-based guidance tailored to your situation, with clear safety-netting before you leave.

faqLibrary.question: What if my dose changes?
faqLibrary.answer: Dose changes need GP update before the pharmacy can supply the new dose. The pharmacy team provides evidence-based guidance tailored to your situation, with clear safety-netting before you leave.

faqLibrary.question: Do I need an appointment for Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Booking ahead for Repeat Prescriptions ensures adequate consultation time. Walk-in availability varies by pharmacy and season — call to confirm same-day capacity.

faqLibrary.question: Is Repeat Prescriptions free on the NHS?
faqLibrary.answer: NHS-funded Repeat Prescriptions is free where the service is commissioned and you meet eligibility criteria. Private repeat prescriptions may incur a disclosed fee confirmed before supply.

faqLibrary.question: How long does a Repeat Prescriptions appointment take?
faqLibrary.answer: Repeat Prescriptions consultations typically take 15–45 minutes depending on assessment complexity, counselling depth and whether tests or supply are involved.

faqLibrary.question: Who is eligible for Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Eligibility for Repeat Prescriptions depends on clinical criteria, age, medical history and local NHS commissioning. Suitability is confirmed individually — not assumed at booking.

faqLibrary.question: What should I bring to my Repeat Prescriptions appointment?
faqLibrary.answer: Bring a complete medicines list, allergy history, relevant test results, travel itinerary if applicable, and photo ID for NHS or controlled services.

faqLibrary.question: Can I speak to a pharmacist before booking Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Yes — a brief phone triage helps confirm whether Repeat Prescriptions is appropriate, explains fees or NHS eligibility, and sets preparation expectations.

faqLibrary.question: What if I am not eligible for Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: If Repeat Prescriptions is not suitable, the pharmacist signposts you to GP, NHS 111, sexual health services or urgent care with documented advice.

faqLibrary.question: How much does private Repeat Prescriptions cost?
faqLibrary.answer: Private repeat prescriptions fees vary by pharmacy and service complexity. Costs are explained before supply — ask for a clear quote at booking.

faqLibrary.question: What happens during a Repeat Prescriptions consultation?
faqLibrary.answer: The pharmacist reviews history, confirms consent, assesses suitability, explains options with risks and benefits, and documents agreed next steps.

faqLibrary.question: When should I see a GP instead of Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Persistent, severe or worsening symptoms, pregnancy complications, systemic illness and emergency presentations need GP or urgent care — not repeat prescriptions alone.

faqLibrary.question: Can I use Repeat Prescriptions for my child?
faqLibrary.answer: Paediatric repeat prescriptions depends on age limits per pathway. Contact the pharmacy to confirm guardian requirements and commissioned paediatric scope.

faqLibrary.question: Is Repeat Prescriptions confidential?
faqLibrary.answer: Yes — Repeat Prescriptions takes place in a private consultation room. Records are held under pharmacy confidentiality and GDPR standards.

faqLibrary.question: What follow-up is needed after Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Follow safety-netting advice, attend booked reviews, and contact the pharmacy or GP if symptoms persist, side effects occur or concerns arise.

faqLibrary.question: Does Repeat Prescriptions require a GP referral?
faqLibrary.answer: Many pharmacy services including repeat prescriptions are self-referral — referral requirements depend on the specific pathway and local commissioning.

faqLibrary.question: How do I book Repeat Prescriptions at the pharmacy?
faqLibrary.answer: Book online, by phone or in person. The team confirms availability, eligibility, fees and preparation instructions for Repeat Prescriptions.

faqLibrary.question: What are the risks of Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Risks depend on the individual and any supplied treatment. The pharmacist explains side effects, contraindications and when to seek urgent help.

faqLibrary.question: Can I get Repeat Prescriptions on the same day?
faqLibrary.answer: Same-day repeat prescriptions may be available for urgent or seasonal services — contact the pharmacy early as appointments fill quickly.

faqLibrary.question: Will my GP be informed after Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Where clinically appropriate, consultation outcomes may be shared with your GP to support continuity — this is explained before proceeding.

faqLibrary.question: What qualifications deliver Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Repeat Prescriptions is delivered by GPhC-registered pharmacists and trained staff under clinical governance, PGDs or protocols where commissioned.

faqLibrary.question: Can I cancel or reschedule Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Yes — contact the pharmacy promptly to reschedule. For time-sensitive services such as emergency contraception, rebook as soon as possible.

faqLibrary.question: Is Repeat Prescriptions better than going to my GP?
faqLibrary.answer: Repeat Prescriptions complements GP care for suitable presentations — it does not replace GP diagnosis or long-term condition management.

faqLibrary.question: What is the difference between NHS and private Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: NHS repeat prescriptions follows commissioned eligibility and may be free; private services offer broader access with disclosed fees and may include options outside NHS scope.

faqLibrary.question: Why choose a pharmacy for Repeat Prescriptions instead of a clinic?
faqLibrary.answer: Community pharmacies offer convenient access, extended hours and integrated medicines expertise — suitable for many patients without hospital referral.

faqLibrary.question: Can I claim Repeat Prescriptions on private medical insurance?
faqLibrary.answer: Insurance coverage for repeat prescriptions varies by policy. The pharmacy provides receipts; check with your insurer before booking.

faqLibrary.question: What if I cannot afford private Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Ask about NHS eligibility or signposting to NHS pathways. The pharmacy team explains free options and alternative services where available.

faqLibrary.question: Is Repeat Prescriptions safe if I take other medicines?
faqLibrary.answer: Bring your full medicines list — the pharmacist checks interactions and contraindications before any supply related to Repeat Prescriptions.

faqLibrary.question: What should I do if Repeat Prescriptions does not work?
faqLibrary.answer: Return for review or see your GP if symptoms persist beyond the expected recovery window explained at your repeat prescriptions consultation.

faqLibrary.question: Can I get Repeat Prescriptions without registering with a GP?
faqLibrary.answer: Some repeat prescriptions services do not require GP registration, but ongoing care usually benefits from GP linkage — confirm locally.

faqLibrary.question: Does Repeat Prescriptions include a written summary?
faqLibrary.answer: Many consultations include written advice or supply labels. Ask for a summary for your records or employer if needed. The pharmacy team provides evidence-based guidance tailored to your situation, with clear safety-netting before you leave.

faqLibrary.question: Are evening or weekend Repeat Prescriptions appointments available?
faqLibrary.answer: Extended hours vary by pharmacy — contact the team for weekend and evening repeat prescriptions availability in your area.

faqLibrary.question: How do I prepare questions for Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Write down symptoms, duration, medicines tried and concerns about cost or eligibility — this helps the pharmacist tailor repeat prescriptions advice.

faqLibrary.question: What red flags mean I should not use Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe bleeding, confusion, stroke symptoms and pregnancy emergencies need urgent care — not routine repeat prescriptions.

faqLibrary.question: Can carers book Repeat Prescriptions for someone else?
faqLibrary.answer: Carers may book on behalf of others with appropriate consent and identification — especially for housebound or vulnerable patients.

faqLibrary.question: Is Repeat Prescriptions suitable if I am pregnant or breastfeeding?
faqLibrary.answer: Pregnancy and breastfeeding affect eligibility for many medicines and services — declare this at assessment for safe repeat prescriptions advice.

faqLibrary.question: How often can I repeat Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Repeat access depends on clinical need and pathway rules — the pharmacist explains appropriate intervals for repeat prescriptions.

faqLibrary.question: What evidence supports Repeat Prescriptions at pharmacies?
faqLibrary.answer: Repeat Prescriptions follows NHS specifications, NICE guidance where applicable, and GPhC professional standards for safe pharmacy-led care.

faqLibrary.question: Will Repeat Prescriptions delay me seeing a specialist?
faqLibrary.answer: Appropriate pharmacy care can resolve suitable cases quickly; referral to GP or specialist occurs when repeat prescriptions falls outside scope.

faqLibrary.question: Can I use Repeat Prescriptions while travelling?
faqLibrary.answer: For travel-related services, bring itinerary dates and previous vaccination records. Non-travel repeat prescriptions is usually locality-based — confirm access.

faqLibrary.question: What languages or accessibility support is available for Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Pharmacies provide reasonable adjustments under equality duties — ask about access needs when booking repeat prescriptions.

faqLibrary.question: Does Repeat Prescriptions include blood tests or screening?
faqLibrary.answer: Some repeat prescriptions pathways include point-of-care tests where equipment is available — confirm what is included when booking.

faqLibrary.question: How is my data used after Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Pharmacy records support safe care and may be shared with your GP where appropriate — privacy is explained at consultation.

faqLibrary.question: What if the pharmacy is closed when I need Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Use NHS 111 for urgent advice when the pharmacy is closed — especially for time-critical services. The pharmacy team provides evidence-based guidance tailored to your situation, with clear safety-netting before you leave.

faqLibrary.question: Can I get a second opinion after Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: You may consult your GP for a second opinion on any repeat prescriptions advice or supply — pharmacy care complements medical review.

faqLibrary.question: Is Repeat Prescriptions available in rural areas near me?
faqLibrary.answer: Community pharmacies serve towns and villages — contact your nearest pharmacy to confirm repeat prescriptions commissioning and booking.

faqLibrary.question: What training do staff have for Repeat Prescriptions?
faqLibrary.answer: Pharmacists complete service-specific training, PGD accreditation and ongoing CPD to deliver Repeat Prescriptions safely.
